Native Coloradoan here. We're currently under a health advisory because the smoke from a wildfire is creating an ugly brown haze over Denver. I've lived here most of my life.

To your question: yes, but it has almost nothing to do with local taxes.

The reaping what we sow is from the 100+ year old policy we've had of immediately extinguishing wildfires. Small periodic wildfires clear out extra fuel while leaving most trees intact. But by putting out every fire, we prevent the forest from removing extra trees, dead branches, and other kindling. The result is that when fires do happen, and we don't contain them in time, they are much more devastating than they otherwise would be.

Policy has shifted, and some fires are now allowed to burn in the right conditions. But old habits die hard, and also, it's not always safe to let fires burn, so it continues.

But it isn't really a matter of local taxes or a lack of equipment. All the equipment in the world isn't going to "put out" an enormous forest fire. The best thing they can do is create a parameter past which the fire can't spread, and that's exactly what they do.
